title: Optimistic Offline Lock

validation.research: Six primary source notes. David Rice is credited for Optimistic Offline Lock in Fowler’s catalog and Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture. Microsoft and SQLAlchemy support version predicates and explicit conflict resolution; SQLite and Python support atomic short transactions and affected-row checks. RFC 9110 supports the second HTTP context with strong ETag/If-Match semantics. Broader optimistic concurrency terminology is distinguished from the offline business-operation lifetime. The example and diagrams are original.
validation.python_examples: Actual notes.py and demo.py fences execute with six stated output lines exactly. Checks cover two independent connection snapshots, conditional version advance, ordered UPDATE/log INSERT/COMMIT, stale and deleted/missing rows, immutable input snapshots, title/ID/version boundaries and exhaustion, later log failure rolling back the title/version, same-title version advance, caller-owned transaction rejection, closed/default connections, and physical contention remaining a storage error. Deliberate unversioned-writer and independent-row read-set cases demonstrate limits.

example_limits: Original immutable Note snapshots and parameterized conditional UPDATE by ID and original version. A successful short SQLite transaction changes title, advances the bounded positive integer version, inserts a local edit-log row, and commits before returning a new snapshot. A stale or deleted row produces Conflict; later log failures roll back all save writes. Two real connections deterministically demonstrate version 1 proposals, version 2 success, stale rejection, and an explicitly reviewed version 3 proposal. No automatic merge/retry, authorization, cross-row read-set validation, token-reset protection, external-effect coordination, or uncertain-commit recovery is implemented.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
